driver: STM32N6 system window watchdog (WWDG) HAL driver (on the verified WWDG LL driver)

source_documents: RM0486 Rev 4 chapter 60 (WWDG) + memory map p.181
target.hsi_contract: RM0486 Rev 4 ch.60 WWDG register interface + memory map p.181 (WWDG secure base 0x50002C00)
target.safety_allocation: NOT_PROVIDED: no owner safety scope recorded for the WWDG work orders

scope: HAL: hal_status_t API with HAL_WWDG_ prefix and a const configuration pointer, built only on the PROVIDED LL_WWDG_ functions

Initialise the watchdog from a configuration (timer base prescaler WWDG_CFR.WDGTB 0..7, window value, counter value, early wake-up interrupt enable): write the prescaler and the window value; with the early wake-up interrupt enabled clear the early wake-up flag, then enable the interrupt (RM0486 60.5); then write the counter and activate the watchdog (the counter with T6 set before WWDG_CR.WDGA, RM0486 60.4.3, 60.4.4)
Refresh: write a counter value to WWDG_CR.T (the caller refreshes inside the window, RM0486 60.4.4)
Query the early wake-up flag (WWDG_SR.EWIF) and clear it (written 0, RM0486 60.6.3)

Parameter checks before any register write, returning HAL_ERROR: a NULL configuration or flag pointer, a prescaler above 7, a window or counter value outside 0x40..0x7F (RM0486 60.4.4, 60.4.5), an early wake-up interrupt selection other than 0 or 1
No HAL_WWDG_ function waits on a WWDG flag (activation, configuration and refresh are register writes; WWDG_SR holds only the early wake-up flag, RM0486 60.6)
Performance: each HAL_WWDG_ call completes within the simulation performance budget
The LL header is provided by a verified WWDG LL work order (--provided-from)

Out of scope: the watchdog reset generation and the early wake-up interrupt handler, the WWDG bus clock enable (RCC), the hardware watchdog option (WWDG_SW), the debug freeze (DBG), a disable or deinit (WWDG_CR.WDGA and WWDG_CFR.EWI are cleared only by a reset, RM0486 60.6.1, 60.6.2)
